verbatim_comment: Please clarify which complete blood count measurement was selected for each patient: the first measurement on admission, a measurement obtained before coronary angiography or the AMI diagnosis, or another measurement during hospitalization. Where possible, the authors should verify the timing of CBC sampling, hospital admission, coronary angiography, the initial AMI diagnosis, and fibrinogen sampling against the original database. If complete timing information is unavailable, the existing measurement-selection rule should at least be stated explicitly.

The accuracy of the AMI diagnostic labels requires further clarification. The authors should explain whether AMI classification was based solely on discharge diagnoses or also incorporated clinical findings, electrocardiography, cardiac biomarkers, or coronary imaging, as applicable. They should also clarify whether the diagnoses underwent any independent clinical review and acknowledge the limitations of the available diagnostic information.

The Methods section states that 2548 patient encounters were initially extracted, yielding 2279 unique patients. The authors should account for the 269 records removed during this process and distinguish repeat admissions from exclusions for other reasons. Furthermore, retaining the admission with the most complete clinical data may affect cohort composition. The authors should explain this selection rule and its rationale and revise the Figure 1 flowchart accordingly.

The internal validation procedure requires further technical clarification. The authors should specify how predictions generated for each patient across 10 repetitions of five-fold cross-validation were aggregated; whether identical outer-fold partitions were used across models; and whether hyperparameter tuning, imputation, and standardization were confined to the training folds. They should also clarify whether the 1,000 bootstrap iterations resampled fixed cross-validated predictions or repeated the entire modeling procedure. This distinction affects the sources of uncertainty represented by the reported 95% confidence intervals.

The temporal sensitivity analysis should be described more precisely. Was the model trained on earlier-period data and evaluated on later-period data, or was cross-validation repeated within the selected temporal sensitivity cohort? These approaches should not be described interchangeably. The authors should report the temporal split point, buffer rules, sample sizes, and numbers of AMI cases. They should also explicitly acknowledge that the difference in AUC between Core-7 and PIV was only 0.002 in this analysis, with a 95% confidence interval that included zero. The modest advantage observed in the primary analysis was therefore not supported to the same extent in the temporal sensitivity analysis.

The primary analysis included 453 patients with AMI, whereas the high-specificity analysis retained only 138 AMI cases. The authors should specify the inclusion and exclusion criteria, explain this substantial reduction in sample size, and clarify whether any eligibility criteria depended on information obtained after the AMI diagnosis. A separate cohort-selection flowchart in the supplementary materials would improve transparency.

The analysis of missing fibrinogen values should be strengthened. In particular, the authors should report fibrinogen missingness separately for the AMI and non-AMI groups and clarify whether the complete-case comparison between Core-7 and Enhanced was performed using identical patients and validation partitions. If these analyses have already been conducted, the existing results and methods should be reported more clearly.

To assess incremental performance more completely, I recommend reporting the AUC, Brier score, and paired differences in AUC for Clinical only, Clinical+PIV, Clinical+Core-7, and Clinical+Enhanced, using the same patients and validation partitions. The authors should also specify how missing clinical variables, including age, hypertension, and diabetes, were handled. Reporting only that Clinical+Core-7 achieved a higher AUC than Clinical+PIV does not fully establish the incremental value of the hematologic models over the baseline clinical model.

The authors should clarify which cross-validated predictions were used to calculate the calibration intercepts and slopes reported in Figure 3 and Table 2. Displaying the distribution of predicted probabilities or the number of patients within each calibration group would also aid interpretation. In addition, the authors should explain why some sensitivity analyses in Figure 5 are presented with AUC point estimates but no 95% confidence intervals.

Finally, the conclusions should reflect the magnitude and robustness of the observed improvements. In the primary analysis, the increase in AUC= 0.017 for Core-7 versus PIV and 0.010 for Enhanced versus Core-7. Both improvements were modest, and the incremental advantage of Core-7 was further attenuated in the temporal sensitivity analysis. The authors should therefore emphasize that jointly modeling routine hematologic measurements provided additional information for AMI phenotype discrimination, rather than suggesting that the model is ready for clinical diagnosis or triage. The existing qualifications in the Discussion should be retained, and the conclusions should be revised consistently after the methodological issues have been addressed.

Authors reporting studies involving humans/human data/the use of human samples must confirm that all experiments were performed in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations. Please ensure that a statement to confirm this has been included in the ‘Ethics approval and consent to participate’ section.

Validation strategy and generalizability
The manuscript describes repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation, but it is unclear whether a formal nested cross-validation procedure was used. Please clarify how the outer validation loop and inner hyperparameter-tuning loop were performed, and whether all preprocessing, imputation, and parameter selection were conducted within the appropriate training folds. Since no independent external cohort appears to have been used, the generalizability of the model remains uncertain. The authors should clarify whether the temporal analysis represents a true temporal validation and moderate claims regarding external applicability.

Potential collinearity among CBC variables
CBC-derived variables may be correlated with each other and with the composite inflammatory indices. Although Elastic-net regression can partly address collinearity, it may still affect variable-selection stability and model interpretation. Please provide a brief assessment of collinearity and discuss the stability of the selected Core-7 variables.

Missing data in clinical variables
The manuscript describes strict handling of missing CBC variables, but it is unclear whether the clinical covariates included in the models also had missing values. Please report the extent of missingness and explain how missing clinical variables were handled. The authors should also clarify whether imputation, if used, was performed within the cross-validation procedure.

Incomplete reporting of composite inflammatory indices
The manuscript states that PIV had the best performance among the conventional composite inflammatory indices, but detailed results for the other indices are not provided. Please report the performance of all prespecified indices, including their AUCs and confidence intervals, and clarify whether Core-7 was compared with each index or only with PIV.

Selection of records for patients with repeated admissions
For patients with repeated hospitalizations, the manuscript states that the most complete record was selected. This approach may introduce selection bias. Please describe how “most complete” was defined and report the number of patients with repeated admissions. The prevalence of prior coronary artery disease, previous myocardial infarction, and prior revascularization should also be reported and their potential role as predictors should be clarified.

Fairness of the comparison with PIV
Core-7 was developed as a multivariable model, whereas PIV appears to have been analyzed as a single continuous variable. Please clarify how PIV was modeled, including whether transformation, standardization, or calibration was applied. All comparator indices should ideally be evaluated using the same validation framework to ensure a fair comparison.

Clinical relevance and comparison with standard biomarkers
The manuscript should better clarify the clinical role of Core-7. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin is the standard biomarker for AMI diagnosis and is generally available within a short time. If troponin data are available, the authors should evaluate whether Core-7 provides incremental value beyond troponin. If troponin was not available, this limitation should be clearly acknowledged, and the authors should explain the specific clinical scenario in which Core-7 would be useful.

Patient selection
The number of included patients over the six-year study period appears relatively low for a tertiary hospital. Please clarify whether patients were screened consecutively. The possibility of selection bias related to data completeness should be discussed.

Timing of CBC measurement
The manuscript should specify when the CBC was collected in relation to hospital admission, symptom onset, troponin testing, coronary angiography, and treatment. If multiple CBC measurements were available, please describe the criteria used to select the index measurement.

Informed consent
The manuscript states that informed consent was obtained from all participants. Please clarify how consent was obtained for the entire study population, particularly given the retrospective design and the fact that the study was conducted in 2026, when some patients may have died or may no longer have been able to provide consent. The authors should specify whether consent was obtained from legally authorized representatives or whether another ethics-approved procedure was used, and ensure that the description is consistent with the ethics approval.

The authors have conducted a comprehensive study to develop multidimensional model to discriminate AMI phenotypes. The research has high methodological quality and provides clinically relevant information. I would suggest to add decision-curve analysis to strengthen the results.
